actions.description: The user stories are code-shaped with real, testable acceptance criteria, correctly distinguish code-shaped stories from documentation-only items rather than forcing everything into a Story template, and are traceable to their BRD/FDD/ADR -- approve them

The user stories have a fundamental, unfixed flaw -- e.g. acceptance criteria that cannot actually be contract-tested, or a story forced into a shape the underlying work does not have -- reject them outright
The user stories need a real change before they can be judged -- distinct from a named, deliberately out-of-scope follow-on item already scoped correctly

metadata.decision_context: Given a drafted epic's user stories, decide whether to approve them, reject them, or request revision -- ADPA's own shape; SocialEngage's alternate (mark_ready/mark_blocked) shape is documented but not initialized, see root-cause-log.md

complexity_profile.rationale: Defaults to true for every policy in this template, learned from a real correction (ADPA's own approve-adr was first built with requires_human_approval: false, and the resolver's own execute_without_confirmation logic would have bypassed a real governance rule as a result). Correct this down per-policy only with real evidence the specific decision doesn't need a human sign-off -- never flip it the other direction speculatively.
